summary.oneLiner: N R Agarwal Industries Limited, founded in 1993, is a Mumbai-headquartered manufacturer of high-quality finished paper and paperboard products for domestic and international markets, producing 4,73,965.40 MT of paper and paperboard in FY 2025-26.
summary.business: The Company manufactures finished paper products from modern manufacturing facilities at Vapi and Sarigam in Gujarat, serving both domestic and international customers. Its product portfolio spans paper used in FMCG packaging, textbooks, print media and notebooks, with a stated focus on innovation, quality improvement and cost efficiency. It is expanding into the packaging board segment through a proposed multilayer board plant.

currentContext.expansion: The Company's principal expansion is a new Multilayer Board Plant (Unit VI), undertaken during FY 2025-26 as a major expansion initiative to expand capacity in the packaging board segment. The proposed plant carries an estimated installed capacity of 1500 tonnes per day and a projected investment of approximately H1,500 Crores. As part of the project the Company has acquired a 4.3 metre deckle board paper machine (2013 make) with a capacity of 1020 TPD, along with pulp stock preparation equipment, and has initiated dismantling and relocation of the machinery to India. Land acquisition has commenced at Dahej, Gujarat, where the Company plans to acquire approximately 150 acres in multiple tranches. The project is expected to be implemented over approximately three years and will be financed by a mix of internal accrual and debt; upon completion it is expected to enhance manufacturing capacity, improve operational efficiencies and strengthen the Company's position in the industry, with the Board continuing to monitor progress. Separately, within existing units the Company upgraded a 5 MW turbine to 6.36 MW within the same footprint, and enhanced the plastic waste boiler to utilise RDF, raising its capacity from 34.5 TPH to 36 TPH and the associated turbine capacity from 7.6 MW to 7.8 MW, together with a sludge drying system that converts dried paper-waste sludge into boiler fuel.

risks.note: The only risk the Company explicitly names anywhere in the routed material: 'A downturn in the economy could weaken consumer spending power, which may translate into lower demand for paper-based products.' Management's stated mitigation is that India's GDP growth of 7.6% in FY 2025-26 reflects resilience and consumption potential, offering wider opportunities despite cyclical pressures. (Read in the Corporate Overview 'Risk management' spread, page 19 — supplied in this workdir's profile/capex bundles, not in the risks bundle itself.)
